result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A is the better reference: its one table gives the token, easing, interrupt behavior and reduced-motion behavior for every pattern, which matches the request closely. B is shorter, has a clearer token table and a better section on changing tokens. However, its recipe table lists raw milliseconds instead of token names, its keyframe examples conflict with its own rule that animations must be interruptible, and its global reduced-motion override doesn't say what the side panel does instead. A's loading and feedback section goes beyond the request and makes it long, and A puts the 'starting point' caveat outside the doc itself. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers define a small token set and map all six patterns to it. A is tighter and easier to use as documentation, and it states plainly that the numbers are starting points to tune at the token level, with design review as the way to propose changes. B gives a better per-pattern reduced-motion breakdown, but it adds loading, feedback, toast policy and error-handling content beyond the request, and it puts the 'starting point' caveat outside the doc itself.
